edge.title: The bag you can't see
edge.setup: You settle into a café with a laptop or phone out, your bag hanging on the chair back or sitting open at your feet. Someone walks past, pauses nearby, maybe asks a question or drops something. You are looking at your screen. Nothing feels wrong.
edge.tell: If your wallet or phone is in a pocket or bag you cannot see or feel, it is available to anyone who walks past.
move: Keep the bag zipped, on your lap or looped through your leg or chair, with the opening facing you, never hanging behind you.
Carry the wallet in a front pocket or an inner zip pocket rather than the top of a bag, and keep only the cards you need that day.
If something is taken, block your cards and UPI from your bank's app straight away, then report it to the police and ask the café for its CCTV before the footage is overwritten.
edge.why: Opportunistic theft needs only a few seconds and a moment of your attention elsewhere. The thief is not beating a lock; they are exploiting the gap between where your valuables are and where you are looking. Close that gap and the theft stops being easy, which is usually enough to send it elsewhere.
edge.variants: Same shape: phones on café tables, bags on the floor of a restaurant, wallets in back pockets on a crowded bus, laptops left 'just for a minute' at a coworking space.
edge.anchor: CCTV shows a woman allegedly stealing a wallet from a customer's bag at a Bengaluru Starbucks, police have reacted (NDTV, India Today).

lens.name: Base rates
lens.one_line: How common something is in general tells you more than how vivid this particular case is.
lens.detail: A horrifying story about one crime says nothing about whether crime rose. Your sense of risk is built almost entirely from stories, and stories are selected for how striking they are, not how typical. The corrective is boring and effective: before reacting, ask what the denominator is.
elsewhere: A startup founder's biography is a sample of one from a pool with a 90% failure rate.
A rare drug side-effect reported in the news, against how many prescriptions.
Plane crash coverage versus the per-kilometre fatality rate.
lens.test: Out of how many? If you can't name the denominator, you don't yet have information — you have an anecdote.
lens.today: Today's Bengaluru feeds lead with an advocate shot dead by tenants over rent in Whitefield, a teen killed by two minors and a woman filmed stealing a wallet at a Starbucks. Each is vivid, and together they feel like a city out of control. None of the reports says how often such things happen, so the feeling is an anecdote until you know the denominator: judge a risk by how common it is, then take the cheap precaution (a zipped bag, a verified tenant) rather than a bigger fear.

carry_over.prompt: A message says your ration card e-KYC must be done today and sends a link: what is the tell?
